status_summary: Executive Order 14155 (signed 2025-01-20) began the WHO withdrawal and paused transfers of funds, and HHS and the State Department announced the withdrawal complete on 2026-01-22. Executive Order 14199 (signed 2025-02-04) ended US participation in the UN Human Rights Council, ended funding for UNRWA, ordered a 90-day UNESCO membership review and ordered a 180-day review of all international organizations and treaties. A State Department statement of 2025-07-22 announced a UNESCO exit effective 2026-12-31. The Rescissions Act of 2025 (Public Law 119-28) rescinded unobligated balances in several international organization accounts. A presidential memorandum signed 2026-01-07 directed agencies to withdraw from 66 organizations (31 UN entities and 35 others), including the UNFCCC, the IPCC, UN Women and UNFPA, and said review of further findings was continuing; the UN depositary recorded the UNFCCC withdrawal notice on 2026-02-27, effective 2027-02-27. The Mandate recommended a review and serious consideration of withdrawal; the 2026 memorandum covers 66 bodies at once, including climate and gender bodies the Mandate did not name.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14155 stated the US intends to withdraw from the WHO, directed a pause in transfers of funds and resources, recall of US personnel working with the WHO, and a halt to negotiation of the WHO Pandemic Agreement (published in the Federal Register 2025-01-29).

Executive Order 14199 ended US participation in the UN Human Rights Council, barred funding to UNRWA, ordered a 90-day review of UNESCO membership, and ordered a 180-day State Department review of all international organizations and treaties with recommendations on withdrawal (published 2025-02-10).

The State Department announces the US will withdraw from UNESCO under Article II(6) of the UNESCO constitution, effective 2026-12-31, with the US a full member until then; the exit is not yet effective as of 2026-10-26.

The Rescissions Act of 2025 (Public Law 119-28) rescinded unobligated balances in international organization accounts, including about $202 million in Contributions to International Organizations, about $361 million in peacekeeping contributions and about $437 million in International Organizations and Programs.

A presidential memorandum directed agencies to take immediate steps to withdraw from 66 organizations (31 UN entities and 35 non-UN bodies), ending participation and, for UN entities, funding to the extent permitted by law; it set no deadline and said review of further findings was ongoing (published 2026-01-16).

HHS and the State Department announce the US has completed its WHO withdrawal, one year after Executive Order 14155; the release says the US stopped WHO funding and withdrew personnel during the year and will coordinate with the WHO only in a limited way to finish the exit.
The UN Secretary-General, as depositary, records the US notification of withdrawal from the UNFCCC, which takes effect for the US on 2027-02-27, one year after receipt.
